## Summary

The project's git history contains two directly relevant commits — one that **introduced** Safari-specific cookie handling, one that **removed** it — plus a "Current state" commit representing the present HEAD. All are in the history of this repository's `src/cookies.cjs`.

### The commits

| Commit | Date | Subject |
|---|---|---|
| `d6d1063c70d5f532b966da0d09d033c29236ec42` | 2024-12-12 10:40 UTC | Work around Safari dropping SameSite=None cookies without Secure |
| `d96b6bb9fb65a28593b34689f5beff7ba6f0dee5` | 2024-12-12 11:40 UTC | Remove the Safari 12.0-12.1 SameSite cookie workaround |
| `3f31cda2879da261ae8117babf9d71e80cdef928` | 2024-12-12 12:40 UTC | Current state (HEAD) |

### Why it was introduced

Commit **`d6d1063`** added the file `src/cookies.cjs` with a user-agent branch. The commit message explains: Safari versions in the **12.0–12.1 range silently drop cookies marked `SameSite=None` even when `Secure` is also set**, due to a known Safari bug. To make the session cookie survive for those users, the code detected those Safari versions via user-agent regex (`/Safari\/12\.[01]/`) and **omitted `SameSite` entirely** for them, returning only `{ secure: true }`, while all other browsers got `{ secure: true, sameSite: 'None' }`:

```js
function cookieAttributesFor(userAgent) {
  if (/Safari\/12\.[01]/.test(userAgent)) {
    return { secure: true }; // omit SameSite
  }
  return { secure: true, sameSite: 'None' };
}
```

The message also noted the intent to "track Safari's fix rollout before removing this branch."

### When and why it was removed

Commit **`d96b6bb`** (one hour later in this fixture history) removed the workaround. The commit message gives two reasons:

1. **Traffic from Safari 12.0–12.1 had been under 0.01% of sessions for two full quarters**.
2. The affected versions were **no longer receiving OS updates**, so users on those versions could not reach the service at all anymore.

The diff deleted the user-agent regex branch and simplified `cookieAttributesFor()` into a parameterless function that always returns `{ secure: true, sameSite: 'None' }`, replacing the branch with a comment: "Safari 12.0-12.1 workaround removed: traffic negligible, versions unsupported."

### Current state

Commit **`3f31cda`** ("Current state", the current HEAD) confirms the working tree is the post-removal state: `src/cookies.cjs` contains only the simplified `cookieAttributesFor()` with no user-agent handling.

**Bottom line:** the special case was introduced (in `d6d1063`) because Safari 12.0–12.1 dropped `SameSite=None` cookies even with `Secure` set, breaking session cookies; it was removed (in `d96b6bb`) once traffic from those versions fell below 0.01% for two consecutive quarters and those versions became unsupported/unable to reach the service.
